Your asking price of $12,600 sits above the KBB fair market range ($10,990–$12,540) and exceeds the estimated private party value (~$11,765). Before we discuss firm numbers, I’ll need to understand what justifies pricing above the market ceiling.

More critically, I need full transparency on the mechanical condition. At nearly 84k miles, this generation of Altima requires careful attention, particularly around the CVT. Please provide documentation for:
- CVT transmission fluid exchange intervals and dates (critical every 30k–60k miles)
- Any history of shifting hesitation, jerking, whining noises, or overheating
- Complete maintenance records for brakes, tires, suspension, steering components, and recent oil/coolant changes
- Any open recalls, dashboard warning lights, or known/lemon-law issues
- Whether the car passes a strict pre-purchase mechanical inspection without reservations

Based on current KBB averages, typical wear at this mileage, and the need to verify CVT health, a realistic starting offer is $9,200, pending your service logs and a clean inspection. Please share the maintenance history and any available photos of the engine bay and undercarriage so we can move forward efficiently.

Looking forward to your response.
